messages.content: Tell me some of the major airports in the United States.

function.name: distance_calculate

message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and overall importance:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest airport in the world by passenger traffic; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major gateway to Asia and Latin America; home to many international carriers. |
| Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD) | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the busiest airports in the U.S.; major hub for United Airlines and American Airlines. |
| Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Large hub for American Airlines; extensive domestic network. |
| Denver International Airport (DEN) | Denver, CO | DEN | Known for its distinctive peaked roof; major hub for United Airlines and Southwest Airlines. |
| John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) | New York City, NY | JFK | Primary international gateway for the East Coast; major hub for JetBlue and Delta. |
| San Francisco International Airport (SFO) | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Key hub for flights to Asia and the Pacific Rim; major hub for United Airlines. |
| Seattle–Tacoma International Airport (SEA) | Seattle, WA | SEA | Major hub for Alaska Airlines and Delta; strong focus on sustainability. |
| Miami International Airport (MIA) | Miami, FL | MIA | Major hub for LATAM and American Airlines; key gateway to Latin America. |
| Orlando International Airport (MCO) | Orlando, FL | MCO | Major hub for Southwest Airlines; serves a large tourist market. |

These airports serve as critical hubs for both domestic and international travel, handling millions of passengers each year.
